summary.text: First page of Web annex 1 (document page 1), tabulating the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes) priority questions and maternal/perinatal outcomes for Section A (Nutritional interventions), covering 1. Dietary interventions (A.1.1 diet/exercise, A.1.2 energy/protein education, A.1.3 balanced energy/protein supplements, A.1.4 high-protein supplementation), 2. Iron and folic acid supplements (A.2.1 daily, A.2.2 intermittent), 3. Calcium supplements (A.3), and 4. Vitamin A supplements (A.4).

sections.title: Page 6

summary.text: Third page of Web annex 1 (document page 3), listing PICO key questions and priority outcomes for Section B.1 (Maternal assessment): 1. Anaemia on-site haemoglobin tests vs full blood count (B.1.1), 2. Asymptomatic bacteriuria Gram stain and dipstick tests vs urine culture (B.1.2), 3. Routine clinical enquiry for intimate partner violence (B.1.3), and four integrated WHO guideline questions covering 4. Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnostic criteria (B.1.4), 5. Tobacco use screening (B.1.5), 6. Alcohol and substance abuse screening (B.1.6), and 7. HIV and syphilis screening (B.1.7), with footnotes citing the source 2013–2015 WHO guidelines.

sections.extract: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience: web annexes 3 Key questions Priority outcomes B. Maternal and fetal assessment B.1. Maternal assessment 1. Anaemia B.1.1: For pregnant women (P), what is the diagnostic value of on-site tests for assessing blood haemoglobin concentration (I) compared with the reference standard (full blood count) (C) to detect maternal anaemia (O)? •

sections.title: Page 7

summary.text: Fourth page of Web annex 1 (document page 4), listing PICO key questions and priority outcomes for maternal tuberculosis screening (B.1.8, integrated from the 2013 WHO TB screening guideline), all five Section B.2 (Fetal assessment) interventions—1. Daily fetal movement counting (B.2.1), 2. Symphysis-fundal height measurement vs clinical palpation (B.2.2), 3. Routine antenatal cardiotocography (B.2.3), 4. Routine early or late fetal ultrasound scan (B.2.4), and 5. Routine Doppler ultrasound of fetal blood vessels (B.2.5)—and the first two Section C (Preventive measures) interventions: 1. Antibiotics for asymptomatic bacteriuria (C.1) and 2. Antibiotic prophylaxis for recurrent UTIs (C.2).

Tuberculosis (TB) B.1.8: For pregnant women (P), does screening women for TB infection in ANC settings (I) compared with not screening for TB (C) improve health outcomes (O)? • Refer to the relevant WHO guideline for the priority outcomes that informed this recommendation5 B.2. Fetal assessment

sections.title: Page 8

summary.text: Fifth page of Web annex 1 (document page 5), listing PICO key questions and priority outcomes for the remaining Section C (Preventive measures) interventions—3. Antenatal anti-D immunoglobulin administration (C.3), 4. Preventive anthelminthic treatment (C.4), 5. Tetanus toxoid vaccination (C.5), 6. Malaria intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (C.6, integrated from the 2015 WHO malaria treatment guidelines), and 7. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention (C.7, integrated from the 2015 WHO ART/PrEP guideline)—plus the first three Section D (Interventions for common physiological symptoms) questions: 1. Nausea and vomiting (D.1), 2. Heartburn (D.2), and 3. Leg cramps (D.3).

sections.title: Page 9

summary.text: Sixth page of Web annex 1 (document page 6), listing PICO key questions and priority outcomes for the remaining Section D physiological symptom interventions—4. Low back and pelvic pain (D.4), 5. Constipation (D.5), and 6. Varicose veins and oedema (D.6)—and the first five Section E (Health system interventions to improve the utilization and quality of ANC) questions: 1. Woman-held case notes (E.1), 2. Midwife-led continuity of care (E.2), 3. Group antenatal care (E.3), 4. Community-based interventions to improve communication and support (E.4), and 5. Task shifting components of ANC delivery (E.5, referencing the 2012 WHO OptimizeMNH guideline).

sections.title: Page 10

summary.text: Seventh and final page of Web annex 1 (document page 7), listing PICO key questions and priority outcomes for the concluding Section E health system interventions: 6. Recruitment and retention of staff in rural and remote areas (E.6, referencing the 2010 WHO rural retention guideline) and 7. ANC contact schedules comparing 4-visit FANC with 8-visit standard care (E.7).

sections.title: Page 11

summary.text: First page of Web annex 2 (document page 8, 'Changes from the approved scope of this guideline'), tabulating PICO questions omitted after approval of the ANC guideline proposal, the reasons for omission, and considerations of potential bias. Covers omitted questions on gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) screening/management and prognostic tests (deferred to a dedicated WHO GDM guideline), home uterine monitoring and vibroacoustic stimulation (excluded as high-risk pregnancy interventions), syphilis diagnostic and prognostic strategies (deferred to a dedicated WHO syphilis screening guideline), and lower genital tract infection screening, prognostic tests, and prophylactic antibiotics (deferred for synthesis within the next five years).

summary.text: Second and final page of Web annex 2 (document page 9), completing the table of PICO questions omitted after guideline scope approval along with reasons and bias assessments: maternal vaccination against Haemophilus influenzae type B and viral influenza (deferred to a specific WHO guideline on vaccinations in pregnancy), interventions to prevent domestic violence/intimate partner violence (excluded as targeting a high-risk subpopulation outside routine ANC scope), and maternal iodine supplementation (deferred pending completion of a dedicated WHO iodine supplementation guideline).
